gap: The date reads 'Mar 14, 25' in a column about 145 px wide, against A's 'Mar…'-free '3:16 AM' at about 95 px. That pushes the excerpt to wrap a word early ('The gale came / up the coast' where A fits 'came up' on one line). The two-digit year '25' also looks like a day of the month sitting next to a day of the month.
gapTheirs: Long names get cut in the middle ('Writing T...riters.txt', 'This is a...lection.txt') because the date column takes the room. B's names all fit whole in the same 340–690 px column, so in A you can't tell what a draft is called at a glance.
verdict: The two panes are nearly identical: the same grounds (#EAEBEB Organizer, #FCFCFC List), the same 136 px row pitch, the same #191919 names and #999999 excerpts and dates, and the same blue bar with no fill. A is the more settled of the two. Its dates stay short, its file icons look like paper, and its window divider is a single hairline. B's divider is twice as heavy, its Recents section holds one item also called 'Recents', and its line-art page icon looks like a system placeholder more than a manuscript. A writer would trust either one, but B still feels like a copy that hasn't been fitted to its own fonts.

states.name: search
states.gap: The list's last row has no closing rule. Under harbour-lights the list just stops: nothing at y≈410–440, where the other side draws a 2 px #EDEDED hairline under every row, the last one included (y≈597). The 2-row result set ends in empty space with no clear end.
states.gapTheirs: Its pane is 1898 px tall where the other is 1800. It stacks 170 px of chrome (traffic lights, a circular back button, a split +/⌄ pill, the Sort pill) above the first row, against 131 px, so the first result name sits at y≈222 instead of y≈182. That leaves 40 px less list on screen before the Filter field.
states.verdict: Both lists are almost the same: rows on a 136 px pitch, names in near-black, excerpts in the same ~#9F grey, a ~127 px cyan bar on the open row and no fill, a #EAEBEB Organizer against a #FCFCFC List with a #CBCCCC divider. A is the finished one. Every row is closed off, the Filter field has its funnel glyph, and the header controls look like buttons. B's list ends without a rule, and its bare sidebar toggle and lone '+' look like placeholders beside a bold centred 'library' title. A writer would trust either with a manuscript, but B looks a pass short of done.
